title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.
key_points: A 175B-parameter decoder-only language model trained to predict the next token.
Learns new tasks from a handful of examples placed in the prompt — in-context learning.
No fine-tuning or weight updates needed to take on a new task.
Showed many capabilities improve smoothly as you scale model size.
Launched the prompting era that shapes how people use LLMs today.
content_html: GPT-3, from Brown, Mann, and colleagues at OpenAI in 2020, is a 175-billion-parameter decoder-only language model. Its headline finding: you can teach it a new task simply by showing a few examples inside the prompt, with no fine-tuning. The paper demonstrated that this "in-context learning" gets stronger as models grow larger.
extra_html:
How it works

GPT-3 is trained on one objective — predict the next token — over a huge text corpus. At use time, you describe the task and optionally include a few worked examples in the prompt itself ("few-shot"). The model conditions on those examples and continues the pattern, effectively learning the task on the fly without any change to its weights.

Why it matters

Before GPT-3, adapting a model to a new task usually meant collecting labeled data and fine-tuning. GPT-3 showed that a big enough model can just be prompted, which made building with LLMs far faster and more flexible. That shift kicked off the prompting era and reframed "programming" an AI as writing good instructions and examples rather than training a new model.

related.title: BERT: Pretraining Deep Bidirectional Transformers
related.hook: What if a model read a sentence both directions at once? BERT did, by masking words and predicting them — and made pretrain-then-fine-tune the default recipe in NLP.

related.title: Chinchilla: Compute-Optimal Scaling
related.hook: Most giant models were starved of data. Chinchilla showed that for a fixed compute budget you should grow parameters and tokens together — and a smaller, longer-trained model won.

related.title: InstructGPT: Aligning LMs with Human Feedback (RLHF)
related.hook: A smaller model people actually like beats a bigger one they don't. InstructGPT used human preferences to make a model follow instructions — the recipe behind ChatGPT.

prereqs.title: Attention Is All You Need
prereqs.hook: Drop recurrence and convolution, keep only attention — and you get a model that trains in parallel and powers nearly every LLM since.
